**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (e.g. your name, school, parentage etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **e)** Life in urban areas is better than life in the rural areas. Give your views.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: the drift from villages to towns and my opinion.
2. Arguments for towns: jobs, social services, entertainment.
3. The other side: costs, crime and pollution against the peace of the village.
4. Way forward: develop rural areas.
5. Conclusion restating my view.

**Model composition (464 words)**

Many people believe that life in towns is better than life in villages, and every year thousands of young Cameroonians leave their villages for cities such as Douala, Yaounde and Bamenda. In my opinion, this view is largely true because towns offer more opportunities, better services and greater comfort, although village life has some real advantages that must not be ignored.

First, urban areas offer far more jobs. Towns have banks, factories, markets, offices, hotels and companies where young people can work and earn a salary. In the village, most people depend on farming, which is hard work and often brings little money because of poor roads and low prices. A graduate who returns to the village may stay unemployed for years, while the same graduate in a city can find a job, start a small business or learn a trade.

Secondly, town dwellers enjoy better social services. Cities have good hospitals with qualified doctors and modern equipment, whereas many villages have only a small health centre which lacks drugs and nurses. Schools, colleges and universities are also concentrated in towns, so children receive a better education there. In addition, towns have electricity, pipe-borne water, telephone networks and the internet, which make life easier and keep people informed about the world.

Thirdly, towns provide entertainment and variety. People can go to cinemas, stadiums, libraries, restaurants and shopping centres, and they meet people from different tribes and countries. This exchange widens the mind and teaches tolerance. Life in the village, by contrast, can be dull and lonely, especially for the young.

However, I must admit that urban life has its own problems. Houses are expensive, and the cost of food, transport and rent is high. Traffic jams, noise and pollution tire people out, and crime such as theft is more common in cities. Many people live in crowded slums without clean water. Rural life, on the other hand, is peaceful and healthy. The air is fresh, food is cheap and straight from the farm, and neighbours know and help one another. These are things money cannot always buy in the city.

Despite these advantages of the village, I still maintain that life in urban areas is better, because the opportunities and services available there improve a person's standard of living. The solution is not to run away from the village but for the government to develop rural areas by building roads, schools, hospitals and markets, and by providing electricity and water. When this is done, villagers will enjoy the same comforts as town dwellers, and the movement from the village to the city will slow down.

In conclusion, although village life is quiet and healthy, towns give people more chances to succeed in life, and for that reason I believe that urban life is better.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Giving no clear opinion, or contradicting oneself, although the topic says "Give your views".
2. Listing arguments without examples or paragraphs, or writing about only one side with no reference to the village.
